rationale: Both nail the PR's core still-live issue (unconditional vllm_c default validated only on Qwen-Image now leaking to ~10+ untested diffusion models, and that Part 2's nn.RMSNorm swap makes Part 1 a no-op for Qwen itself) with near-identical evidence, and both independently flag the ROCm/XPU sibling gap and the module-scope test import risk. Y edges ahead on precision: it grounds essentially every claim in file:line/grep citations, explicitly re-validates the pytest-mark and 'UT added' threads that match the ground-truth comment history almost exactly, and catches a genuine, independently-verifiable arithmetic error in the PR's own FLUX benchmark table. X's 'What I verified' section includes suspiciously over-specific runtime claims (exact tensor strides, GPU test pass counts) with no supporting trace, which is a fabrication risk that Y avoids by hedging honestly where it can't verify (e.g., the AMD-CI claim).
